title: Surveillance Sensor Operator (MSgt to Pvt) NMOS (0231, 0311, 0369, 0399, 0621, 0629, 2651), DIR INTEL
raw_text:
1. MOS 8621, Surveillance Sensor Operator (MSgt to Pvt) NMOS (0231, 0311,
0369, 0399, 0621, 0629, 2651), DIR INTEL

    a. Summary. Surveillance Sensor Operators inspect, install, and operate
remote, unattended, Measurement and Signals Intelligence (MASINT) and imaging
sensors, in support of intelligence collection and MAGTF operations. As a
part of surveillance and reconnaissance missions, sensors are frequently
employed in places too dangerous to maintain personnel or where it is not
tactically practical to deploy other surveillance systems. Remote sensors
use multiple sensing and radio communications methods to detect and report
personnel and vehicle activity in designated areas of interest. Patrolling,
navigation, camouflage, communication, and infantry tactics are required by
the sensor operator. Additionally, sensor operators must be able to perform
operator maintenance on surveillance equipment prior to and after employment.
In addition the following skill sets are recommended for Surveillance Sensor
Operators application of tactical C2 systems, map reading, terrain
association, radio operations, antenna propagation, radio waves, spectrum
management, weather observation., imagery/video analysis, and operational
risk management.

       b.    Prerequisites

             (1) Must possess a GT score of 100 or higher.

             (2) Must have normal color vision and depth perception.

             (3) Must have a 1st class physical fitness and combat fitness test
score.

        (4) Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility (not
required for Surveillance Sensor Operators Course (SSOC) attendance).

    c. Requirements. Must complete the USMC Sensor Surveillance Operator
Course (N46BGK2) located at the Marine Corps Detachment Dam Neck, VA.

       d.    Duties

        (1) Prepares various types of remote sensor surveillance devices for
air and hand emplacement methods in areas previously determined.

        (2) Monitors and interprets sensor devices by analyzing and
evaluating sensor data.

             (3) Plan and plot device locations on maps and overlays.

        (4) Makes recommendations to and assists the intelligence officer in
selecting areas, routes, and specific emplacement sites and sensor/ device
type.

        (5) Provides timely and accurate data concerning enemy location,
direction, speed of movement, and size.

        (6) Assists in testing and evaluating new sensor surveillance
equipment and ancillary devices.

             (7) Provides surveillance equipment instruction.



                                         3-498                          Enclosure (1)
 3153                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



        (8) Perform operator and preventive maintenance on all sensor
equipment.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Radar and Sonar Technicians 55-3017.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Rifleman, 0311.

            (2) Transmissions System Operator, 0621.

Operate airborne remote sensing equipment, such as survey cameras, sensors, or scanners.
Remote sensors use multiple sensing and radio communications methods to detect and report personnel and vehicle activity in designated areas of interest.
Install, calibrate, or maintain sensors, mechanical controls, GPS-based vehicle guidance systems, or computer settings.
Patrolling, navigation, camouflage, communication, and infantry tactics are required by the sensor operator.
Observe work and monitor gauges, dials, and other indicators to ensure that operators conform to production or processing standards.
Additionally, sensor operators must be able to perform operator maintenance on surveillance equipment prior to and after employment.
Install, calibrate, or maintain sensors, mechanical controls, GPS-based vehicle guidance systems, or computer settings.

In addition the following skill sets are recommended for Surveillance Sensor Operators application of tactical C2 systems, map reading, terrain association, radio operations, antenna propagation, radio waves, spectrum management, weather observation., imagery/video analysis, and operational risk management.
Operate airborne remote sensing equipment, such as survey cameras, sensors, or scanners.

Must complete the USMC Sensor Surveillance Operator Course (N46BGK2) located at the Marine Corps Detachment Dam Neck, VA. d. Duties (1) Prepares various types of remote sensor surveillance devices for air and hand emplacement methods in areas previously determined.
Process or interpret signals or sensor data.
(2) Monitors and interprets sensor devices by analyzing and evaluating sensor data.
Produce or update overlay maps to show information boundaries, water locations, or topographic features on various base maps or at different scales.
(3) Plan and plot device locations on maps and overlays.
Install, calibrate, or maintain sensors, mechanical controls, GPS-based vehicle guidance systems, or computer settings.
(4) Makes recommendations to and assists the intelligence officer in selecting areas, routes, and specific emplacement sites and sensor/ device type.
Operate counters and record data to assess the volume, type, and movement of vehicular or pedestrian traffic at specified times.
(5) Provides timely and accurate data concerning enemy location, direction, speed of movement, and size.
Conduct surveillance testing to determine safety of nuclear equipment.
(6) Assists in testing and evaluating new sensor surveillance equipment and ancillary devices.
Direct installation of covert surveillance equipment, such as security cameras.
(7) Provides surveillance equipment instruction.
Perform maintenance tasks necessary to keep equipment working properly.
(8) Perform operator and preventive maintenance on all sensor equipment.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
